item.title: Sewer cover faulty, 13th September
item.description:
I would like to report an issue with a drain cover adjacent to our property on what we understand is land owned by the Highways agency. The drain is on an access path to 6 Sudeley View Winchcombe GL545NB. I have attached pictures of the drain and a copy of a map diagram from the Highways Agency sent to us during a previous interaction. As can be seen from your map the footpath and bank abutting the property are indicated as belonging to the Highways Agency. Please note that the property numbering is incorrect on your diagram and 6 Sudeley View is actually the end cottage in a row of six and not located to the rear of 5 Sudeley View. Please also note that the access path is also used to gain entry to the rear of 5 Sudeley View as well as 6 Sudeley View. For clarification, 6 Sudeley View has no front access. Regarding the drain cover; it appears the frame that the cover is sat on is not one solid frame but four separate pieces, one of these pieces (longer edge) is missing and may have fallen away into the drain. The drain cover is no longer flush with the path surface and looks to be sinking below. This cause a bit of a trip hazard but more importantly concern that it might collapse under weight and cause injury. The drain covers here (there is a second one on the path and one in the rear yard were all lifted last year by Severn Trent during inspection work in the road and properties locally. Please could the drain cover be inspected and repaired accordingly. Kind regards

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Gloucester Street, Winchcombe, Winchcombe, Tewkesbury

item.title: 3 way temp traffic lights, 13th September
item.description:
Work has now commenced on the pavements along Farm Lane, including the installation of temporary three-way traffic lights. While we understand that some disruption is inevitable while the work is being carried out, it is extremely frustrating that once work has finished for the day — and particularly at weekends when no work is taking place — the traffic lights, cones and associated equipment are simply left in place. This means residents are having to negotiate temporary traffic lights day after day, even when there appears to be no active work taking place. I live on the Lanes, and residents have endured roadworks, temporary traffic lights and associated disruption for nearly five years now. Quite frankly, we are fed up with it. Could you please ask the contractors to remove the traffic lights and as much of the temporary equipment as reasonably possible at the end of each working day, particularly over weekends when there is no work taking place? We appreciate that some restrictions may be necessary for safety reasons, but where they are not required outside working hours, there seems little justification for leaving them in place and causing residents unnecessary inconvenience. I would appreciate it if the council could raise this with the contractors and ask them to minimise the disruption to residents wherever possible. Kind regards, Grant
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Farm Lane, Warden Hill, Cheltenham
Report on FixMyStreet
